### 3. ci-hosted-shard-duration-balancing

| Field | Content |
|---|---|
| Route | `direct` |
| Diagnosis | Re-derived against live source 2026-09-02 (this session). The row's original "rebalance the shards" framing is refuted by its own evidence gate, and the surviving defect is durability of the calibration, not the partition. `CI_POLICY.md:78` still instructs a future reader to "Use complete green four-shard hosted runs as the next calibration and rebalance only from repeated uploaded TRX evidence" — but that evidence lives in GitHub artifacts with a 14-day retention (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`), so the calibration is un-re-checkable and the next reader is pushed toward exactly the single-sample or local-timing mistakes acceptance bullets 1 and 3 forbid. There is no offline, deterministic tool that turns downloaded `test-results-<leg>` folders into a per-image skew report: `eng/summarize-test-results.ps1` has the TRX parsing (`Read-TrxCases` at `:97`, `Get-TimingAggregates` at `:185`) but is a single-run job-summary renderer with no image partitioning and no minimum-sample gate. Acceptance bullet 4 is ALREADY satisfied for the static planner by `tests/RoslynMcp.Tests/TestShardPlanContractTests.cs:60-90` (completeness, disjointness, non-empty shards, greedy-balance bound across 1/2/4 shards), `:99-157` (missing/unreadable/zero-class fail-closed) and `:243-279` (stale external catalog, both drift directions). |
| Approach | Acceptance bullets, verbatim from `ai_docs/items/ci-hosted-shard-duration-balancing.md`: (1) Collect at least five successful per-leg TRX runs for each hosted OS/image and quantify wall-time skew separately from summed case duration. (2) Adopt duration weights only when repeated evidence shows material skew; keep deterministic discovered-case weights as a fail-closed fallback. (3) Model hosted Windows and hosted Linux independently; do not mix local-machine timings into either profile. (4) One deterministic missing/stale-profile regression proves no class is omitted, overlapped, or assigned to an empty shard. Implementation: (a) new `eng/collect-hosted-shard-timings.ps1` — offline, deterministic, taking a directory of downloaded `test-results-<leg>` folders plus leg metadata (leg, hosted image, wall-time seconds, run id); mirror the TRX parsing in `eng/summarize-test-results.ps1:97`/`:185`; partition strictly by hosted image, refuse to merge images or accept an untagged leg, require `-MinimumSamples` (default 5) and fail closed below it; emit wall-time skew and summed case duration as SEPARATE columns plus per-leg run-to-run spread and the achievable-gain figure; no `gh` call inside the script. (b) Rewrite the open "next calibration" sentence at `CI_POLICY.md:78` with the measured outcome, the achievable-gain ceiling, the explicit decision that static discovered-case weights remain the fail-closed weighting, and the re-check trigger. (c) Record the collector in the evidence table at `ai_docs/references/testing.md:17-31`, plus a bullet stating that summed TRX case duration alone is not a partition signal on hosted runners. (d) Extend `tests/RoslynMcp.Tests/TestResultsSummaryContractTests.cs` with deterministic collector regressions over TRX synthesized under `TestTempRoot.Current` (pattern at `TestShardPlanContractTests.cs:240-269`). |

### 4. formatter-baseline-generator-concurrent-load-timeout

| Field | Content |
|---|---|
| Route | `direct` |
| Diagnosis | Re-derived against live source 2026-09-02 (this session). The five-minute bound is not the defect — the blindness around it is. `tests/RoslynMcp.Tests/FormatterBaselineContractTests.cs` declares `_processTimeout = TimeSpan.FromMinutes(5)` at `:19`; on expiry `:274-287` kills the process tree and throws a `TimeoutException` carrying only the bound, while the `stdoutTask`/`stderrTask` started at `:275-276` are ABANDONED — the killed generator's partial output, the only evidence of where it stalled, is discarded at exactly the moment it is needed. `eng/generate-format-baseline.ps1` runs `dotnet restore` (`:81-88`) then `dotnet format` (`:91-93`) back-to-back with no phase marker or elapsed time, so even captured output could not separate restore contention from format contention. That is precisely the 2026-09-01 evidence: a required `just ci` retry timed out at five minutes while another repository testhost was active, and the same test passed in 49 seconds once the competing testhosts exited. `eng/format-diagnostic-contract.ps1` is the 4-line shared grammar file (`$formatDiagnosticPattern`, `$formatTruncationMarker`) both emitter and parser dot-source. |
| Approach | Acceptance bullets, verbatim from `ai_docs/items/formatter-baseline-generator-concurrent-load-timeout.md`: (1) Distinguish a generator hang from host-wide MSBuild/dotnet-format contention with bounded operator-visible diagnostics. (2) Prove the generator contract completes or fails with an actionable classification under concurrent repository build/test load. (3) Preserve the five-minute safety bound unless repeated evidence justifies a measured replacement; do not hide contention by only increasing the timeout. Implementation — add signal, not slack; `_processTimeout` stays at 5 minutes verbatim: (a) `eng/format-diagnostic-contract.ps1` gains one shared `$formatPhaseMarkerPrefix` alongside the existing two variables, so emitter and parser share one grammar; (b) `eng/generate-format-baseline.ps1` emits `restore start|end` and `format start|end` markers with elapsed ms on stderr around `:81-88` and `:91-93`; (c) `FormatterBaselineContractTests.cs` `RunGeneratorCheckAsync` (`:249-290`) snapshots competing processes before `Process.Start` and again on timeout (`dotnet`/`testhost`/`MSBuild`/`VBCSCompiler`, excluding this pid and the generator tree, per-process `Win32Exception` swallowed, capped at 10), DRAINS the already-started read tasks under a bounded wait after `Kill(entireProcessTree: true)` instead of abandoning them, extracts a testable pure static `ClassifyGeneratorTimeout(...)` returning `generator-never-started` / `generator-hang` / `host-contention`, and puts that verdict plus per-phase elapsed and the competing-process list in the `TimeoutException` message; the same phase-timing line is emitted on the SUCCESS path so TRX runs accumulate the repeated evidence bullet 3 requires before any measured bound replacement. |
| Scope | Production 2: `eng/generate-format-baseline.ps1`, `eng/format-diagnostic-contract.ps1`. Tests 1 extended: `tests/RoslynMcp.Tests/FormatterBaselineContractTests.cs`. No Rule 3 exemption claimed — 2 of 4. |
| Tool policy | `edit-only` |
| Estimated context cost | 35000 |
| Risks | **Hard constraint:** generator STDOUT is the byte-compared determinism payload (`FormatterBaselineContractTests.cs:211-214`) — every new diagnostic MUST go to stderr or the determinism assertion breaks. **Second hard constraint:** use raw `[Console]::Error.WriteLine`, NOT `Write-Error` — `$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'` at `generate-format-baseline.ps1:49` would abort the script. Markers must not enter `$formatOutput` (`:92` merges only the `dotnet format` child's stderr), leaving the truncation check at `:103-106` and the JSON payload untouched. Fanout probe: 4 consumers dot-source the shared contract; only the generator must change (`eng/verify-changed-format.ps1` dot-sources and ignores the additive variable; `tests/RoslynMcp.Tests/Skills/ChangedFormatGateScriptTests.cs` asserts on the gate's own streams) — so `fanoutEstimate` 4 against 2 production files stays inside Rule 5b's `+2` band. **Bad code fixed by this row (Directive #3):** `FormatterBaselineContractTests.cs:274-287` abandons `stdoutTask`/`stderrTask` on the timeout throw path. **Deliberately deferred — do NOT do it in this PR:** the test pays two full `dotnet restore` passes because `RunGeneratorCheckAsync` omits `-NoRestore`; dropping restore weakens the fail-closed truncation contract at `:103-106`, and it is exactly the "measured replacement" the new success-path timings are meant to justify. Tracked by row `formatter-baseline-generator-double-restore-cost`. |

### 5. test-base-static-service-locator-decomposition

| Field | Content |
|---|---|
| Route | `direct` |
| Diagnosis | Re-derived against live source 2026-09-02 (this session). The immutable fixture context this row asks for ALREADY EXISTS: `tests/RoslynMcp.Tests/TestInfrastructure/TestServiceContainer.cs` is a 312-line `internal sealed class` holding 63 `required`/`init` service members behind a single `Create(ValidationServiceOptions)` factory. The defect is the copy layer on top of it — `tests/RoslynMcp.Tests/TestBase.cs:162` builds the container once, then hand-copies every member into 67 mutable `protected static … { get; private set; }` declarations (verified count: 67 in the live file). Every new service is written twice inside `TestBase.cs` plus once in the container; that is the "obscures ownership" symptom the row names. Three unrelated concerns are welded to the same class: repository fixture paths (declared ~`:113-116`, discovered ~`:232-236`), MCP path-authorized server ownership (`_pathAuthorizedServerTask` at `:15`), and assembly disposal (`DisposeAssemblyResourcesAsync` from ~`:257`, hand-rolled because `TestServiceContainer` does not implement `IDisposable`; `AssemblyCleanup.cs:11-16` calls it from `AssemblyLifecycle.Cleanup` under `[AssemblyCleanup]`). **Anchor correction (Directive #5):** the row's `## Anchors` cites `tests/RoslynMcp.Tests/TestServiceContainer.cs`, which does not exist — the type lives at `tests/RoslynMcp.Tests/TestInfrastructure/TestServiceContainer.cs`. The Anchors block also omits `tests/RoslynMcp.Tests/IsolatedWorkspaceTestBase.cs` (221 lines, the load-bearing derived base) while citing the 8-line `SharedWorkspaceTestBase.cs`. |
| Approach | Acceptance bullets, verbatim from `ai_docs/items/test-base-static-service-locator-decomposition.md`: (1) Replace the dozens of mutable static service properties with one immutable, assembly-owned fixture context constructed from `TestServiceContainer`. (2) Separate repository fixture paths and assembly lifecycle ownership from service lookup so initialization and disposal have one explicit owner. (3) Preserve the assembly-shared workspace behavior and source-compatible class cleanup boundary while migrating consumers incrementally or atomically. (4) Add one parallel two-class regression proving both classes receive the same initialized context and that its owned resources are disposed exactly once. Implementation — forwarder-preserving variant: new `tests/RoslynMcp.Tests/TestInfrastructure/TestAssemblyFixture.cs` exposing `Services` (the existing container), a `TestRepositoryFixtures` record for the repository/fixture paths, and the lazy `McpRootsTestServerFactory.Session`; it implements async disposal, absorbing `DisposeAssemblyResourcesAsync` so disposal gets exactly one owner. `TestBase.cs` replaces the mutable statics and their assignment block with one `_fixture` field plus 67 get-only expression-bodied forwarders. `InitializeServices()` keeps its `_initLock` double-checked once-per-assembly contract verbatim; `AssemblyCleanup.cs` needs no edit. |
| Scope | Production 0 — every file is under `tests/`. Test files 3 (exactly at the Rule 4 cap): `tests/RoslynMcp.Tests/TestBase.cs` (modified), `tests/RoslynMcp.Tests/TestInfrastructure/TestAssemblyFixture.cs` (new), `tests/RoslynMcp.Tests/TestAssemblyFixtureTests.cs` (new — two parallel `[TestClass]`es proving both observe the same fixture reference and owned resources dispose exactly once, acceptance bullet 4). |
| Tool policy | `edit-only` |
| Estimated context cost | 45000 |
| Risks | **Fanout probe (re-run 2026-09-02, decisive for sizing): 160 test files derive from the `TestBase` hierarchy and reference at least one of the 67 inherited static members.** REJECTED variant — atomic migration (delete the statics, make consumers say `Fixture.Services.X`): edits 160 test files, ~53x over Rule 4 and over Rule 5; it must NOT be substituted at execute time. CHOSEN variant works because all 160 consumers use the *unqualified inherited name*, which a get-only forwarder preserves byte-for-byte — so the compile of all 160 consumers IS the source-compatibility proof, and `fanoutEstimate` stays at 3 changed files. **Behavioral risk:** `IsolatedWorkspaceTestBase.cs:113` and `:142` capture `WorkspaceManager.Close`/`LoadAsync` through the inherited static in a nested type's constructor chain — keep the forwarder's null surface identical to today's or assert eagerly. **Build-order:** this initiative is scheduled in its own later generation (`dependsOn` the other four) because `TestBase.cs` is the compile root of the whole test assembly; the file-overlap graph cannot see that edge, and landing it last means its own CI gate compiles every sibling's newly added test file. **Residual accepted by design:** 67 forwarder declarations remain in `TestBase.cs`, so adding a service still touches it once (down from twice); eliminating that last hop needs the 160-file migration and belongs to a separate row. |
